name: nlp_reranker_bad
title: A cross-encoder reranker whose pooling stack lives in a plain list, whose sigmoid head is fed to BCEWithLogitsLoss, whose training loader never shuffles and whose entrypoint runs at import time with four worker processes
origin: hardening round 2, domain-nlp, 2026-09-14 - the ranking/reranking shape, and a second probe of the module-scope entrypoint that MLV112 exists for
note: Eight planted defects, eight modelled by a rule, six found today. The two misses are MLV402 - the double sigmoid, whose producing chain ends in .squeeze(-1) rather than in the nn.Sigmoid and then crosses a subtraction - and MLV112, which only looks one call level below module scope even though main() is called at module scope on line 75 (NLP2-07).

expected.defect: the pooling stack is a plain Python list, so nn.Module never registers its parameters
expected.why: self.blocks[0] is a Linear with 384x384 weights that the optimizer never sees and state_dict never saves, and nothing raises: the reranker simply never learns that layer

expected.defect: the model already applies nn.Sigmoid (line 20) and the pairwise loss is BCEWithLogitsLoss, which applies it again
expected.why: the margin fed to the loss is a difference of two probabilities in (-1, 1), so the loss saturates at a near-constant value and the ranking barely moves

expected.defect: nothing seeds torch, numpy or python random
expected.why: the split, the dropout masks and the head initialisation all move between runs

expected.defect: torch.load passes neither map_location= nor weights_only=
expected.why: the triples file is unpickled with full code-execution rights, and the load fails outright on a machine without the device it was written from
the evaluation triples change on every run, so two nDCG numbers from two runs are not comparable

expected.defect: the training loader has neither shuffle=True nor a sampler
expected.why: random_split preserves the underlying order, so every epoch sees the triples in the same corpus order and consecutive batches are correlated

expected.defect: num_workers=4 in a module whose last statement is a bare main() call (line 75) with no if __name__ == "__main__" guard
expected.why: under spawn every worker re-imports train_reranker.py, which calls main() again, which spawns four more workers - the run never starts

expected.defect: the same missing __main__ guard, seen from a second loader
expected.why: LABEL ADDED in hardening round 2: the eval loader requests the same four workers from the same unguarded module (the `expected` row at line 23 is the training loader). One guard fixes both, so this is `acceptable`.

expected.defect: the epoch loss accumulates the tensor rather than loss.item()
expected.why: LABEL CORRECTED in hardening round 2 (finding VIS2-09): a workspace `nn.Module` loss class now earns the LOSS tag from its own structure - it registers no submodules and its body reduces a tensor - so MLV205 can type the value. Original note: MLV205 models exactly this, but it cannot type a loss produced by a workspace nn.Module criterion (PairwiseLoss) - see NLP2-09; recorded as unsupported so the same hole is not counted twice

expected.symbol: for positive_ids, positive_mask, negative_ids, negative_mask in loader
expected.why: CrossEncoder carries nn.Dropout(0.1) in its pooling stack, so the nDCG@10 printed after every epoch is measured through a randomly thinned network

expected.symbol: for positive_ids, positive_mask, negative_ids, negative_mask in loader
expected.defect: evaluate() is not wrapped in torch.no_grad() and carries no decorator
expected.why: two transformer forwards per batch keep their graphs alive for the whole evaluation

expected.defect: the device is hard-coded to cuda with no availability check
expected.why: the script cannot be smoke-tested on a CPU box

forbidden.why: optimizer.zero_grad() is the first statement of the batch loop (line 32)
there is no torch.no_grad() block anywhere in this project - that absence is MLV302's finding
get_linear_schedule_with_warmup is a per-batch schedule and scheduler.step() runs inside the batch loop (line 38), which is correct
no gradient clipping call exists in this project, so none can be in the wrong position
the evaluation loader leaves shuffle at its default False (line 24)
no CrossEntropyLoss is constructed here; the objective is BCEWithLogitsLoss, whose sigmoid mismatch is MLV402's finding
every one of the four batch tensors gets an explicit .to(device) at the forward (lines 34-35 and 46-47)
both nn.Module subclasses call super().__init__() (lines 16 and 34)
ndcg_at_k ranks scores with torch.argsort (reranker.py line 43); it is a ranking metric and takes scores by design
no roc_auc_score / average_precision_score appears in this project
no sklearn transformer is fitted anywhere in this project
there is no HuggingFace Trainer here - the loop is hand-written
there is no Keras code in this project

unsupported.defect: the ideal gains are divided by the *retrieved* order's discounts rather than by their own, so nDCG is wrong whenever fewer than k documents are returned
unsupported.why: no rule models the arithmetic of a ranking metric

unsupported.defect: none - TensorDataset is a framework class with both dunder methods
unsupported.why: MLV115 is a later-tier rule and is not built

unsupported.defect: the checkpoint is written after the loop rather than when the nDCG improves, so a mid-run peak is lost
unsupported.why: MLV802 is a later-tier rule and is not built
